p.seg: Bǎi Hé Dì Yī
Examining antiquity,
the sage in this world
takes precedence over all living beings.
He observes the opening and closing of yin and yang to determine the fate of things.
He understands the gateway to survival and destruction.
He plans and calculates the beginning and end of all categories.
He comprehends the principles of the human heart.
He sees the signs of change,
and guards and oversees its gateway.
Therefore, the sage in this world,
from ancient times to the present,
his way is one and the same.
Changes are endless,
each having its own destination.
Sometimes yin, sometimes yang,
sometimes soft, sometimes firm,
sometimes open, sometimes closed,
sometimes relaxed, sometimes tense.
Therefore, the sage solely guards and oversees this gateway,
carefully examines what comes first and what comes after,
assesses power and measures ability,
compares their skills, strengths, and weaknesses.
For the worthy, the unworthy, the wise, the foolish, the brave, the cowardly, benevolence and righteousness, there are differences.
Thus, one can open;
Then it can be closed;
then it can be advanced;
then it can be retreated;
then it can be debased;
and it can be ennobled;
govern them through non-action (*wúwéi*).
Carefully determine existence and non-existence,
and verify their reality and emptiness.
Follow their likes and dislikes to observe their ambitions and intentions,
subtly refute what they say,
and open and close in opposition to it,
in order to seek the truth,
valuing obtaining its essence.
Close and then open it,
in order to seek its benefit.
Sometimes open it and show it,
sometimes close it and shut it.
Opening it and showing it means
to accord with their emotions;
closing it and shutting it means
to differentiate their sincerity.
Whether acceptable or unacceptable,
carefully clarify their plans,
in order to investigate their similarities and differences.
Separation and union must have principles,
and first follow their ambitions.
If you wish to open, value thoroughness;
Namely, the shutting relies on valuing secrecy.
The carefulness of being thorough relies on valuing subtlety,
and thus corresponds with the Dao.
Those who *bǎi* consider the feelings [of others];
those who *hé* consolidate their sincerity.
If one perceives the weight and importance of their power,
then one measures accordingly.
The sage thereby contemplates for them.
If it does not accord with measurement and calculation,
the sage thereby contemplates for himself.
Therefore, *bǎi* is,
either *bǎi* to release it,
or *bǎi* to draw it in.
*Hé* is, either *hé* to take it,
or *hé* to let it go.
*Bǎi hé* is the Dao of Heaven and Earth.
*Bǎi hé* is used to transform *yīnyáng*,
the opening and closing of the four seasons,
to transform the myriad things in their vertical and horizontal dimensions.
Reversals, advances and retreats, opposition,
necessarily arise from this.
*Bǎi hé* is the great transformation of the Dao,
the alteration of persuasion.
One must beforehand examine its transformations.
The mouth is the gate of the heart;
the heart is the master of the spirit (*shén*).
Intentions, desires, thoughts, and wisdom,
All (affairs) come out and enter through doorways.
Therefore, they are controlled by *bāihé* (opening and closing),
and regulated by exiting and entering.
*Bāi* means opening,
speaking,
*yáng*.
*Hé* means closing,
silence,
*yīn*.
When *yīn* and *yáng* are harmonized,
beginnings and endings have their proper meaning.
Therefore, speaking of longevity, peace and happiness, wealth and honor, esteem and glory, prominent reputation, love and desire, riches and benefits, fulfillment, joy and desire, all are *yáng*,
called "beginning."

Therefore, speaking of death, worries and troubles, poverty and lowliness, bitterness and disgrace, abandonment and loss, lost profits, disappointment, harm, criminal punishment, execution and penalties are *yīn*,
called "ending."
All speech that follows the *yáng* category,
is called "beginning,"
speaking of goodness to begin the affair;
all speech that follows the *yīn* category,
is called "ending,"
speaking of evil to end the plan.
The *bāihé* way
uses *yīn* and *yáng* to test (things);
therefore, when speaking with *yáng*, rely on the lofty and high,
when speaking with *yīn*, rely on the humble and small.
Use the low to seek the small,
use the high to seek the large.
From this perspective,
there is nowhere it does not emerge,
nowhere it does not enter,
nowhere it is not applicable.
It can be used to speak of individuals,
it can be used to speak of families,
it can be used to speak of states,
it can be used to speak of the world.
In smallness, there is no interior;
in greatness, there is no exterior.
Increase and decrease, acceptance and rejection, doubling and reversal,
all are governed by *yīnyáng* in their affairs.
*Yáng* moves and acts,
*yīn* rests and conceals;
*yáng* moves and exits,
*yīn* follows and enters.
*Yáng* cycles through to completion;
when *yīn* reaches its extreme, it reverts to *yáng*.
When *yáng* moves,
virtue arises reciprocally;
when *yīn* is still,
forms are completed reciprocally.
When *yáng* seeks *yīn*,
it embraces with virtue;
when *yīn* binds *yáng*,
it exerts force;
*yīn* and *yáng* seek each other,
through opening and closing (*bǎihé*).
This is the way of *yīnyáng* of Heaven and Earth,
and the method of speaking to people,
preceding all matters.
This is called "the gateway of roundness and squareness."
Response, Chapter Two
The great transformers of ancient times
were born together with the formless.
Use *fǎn* to observe the past,
use *fù* to verify the future;
use *fǎn* to know the ancient,
use *fù* to know the present;
use *fǎn* to know the other,
use *fù* to know oneself.
The principles of movement and stillness, emptiness and fullness,
if they do not accord with present times,
seek them by reverting to antiquity.
Matters for which reversal (*fǎn*) can yield verification (*fù*)
are the intent of the sage,
and must not be overlooked.
The speech of others is movement;
one's own silence is stillness.
Based on their speech,
listen to their words.
If there are inconsistencies in their speech,
seek them out by reversing (*fǎn*),
and the response will surely emerge.
Words have images;
affairs have comparisons.
When there are images and comparisons,
examine them to observe their order.
"Images" image the affairs;
"comparisons" compare the words.
Using the formless to seek the voiced,
their baiting words will align with the affair,
and you will obtain the person's truth.
When spreading nets to capture beasts,
spread many meeting points and oversee them.
If the Dao aligns with the affair,
they will come forth on their own.
This is the net for fishing people.
Constantly hold your net and drive them,
and if their words lack comparison,
then change tactics for them,
using images to move them,
to repay their hearts,
to see their true feelings,
and then follow and shepherd them.
When you go back,
they will repeatedly come.
When words have images and comparisons,
then establish a firm foundation based on this.
Layer them and repeat them.
Reverse it and overturn it.
In ten thousand affairs, you will not lose their wording.
The sage uses enticements on both the foolish and the wise,
and in these matters, nothing is doubted.
The ancients who were skilled at "reverse listening"
could even transform ghosts and spirits in order to obtain their true feelings.
If their transformations were appropriate,
then their guidance (of the situation) was accurate.
If their guidance was inaccurate,
obtaining the true feelings would be unclear.
If obtaining the true feelings is unclear,
establishing a firm foundation will be inaccurate.
When transforming appearances and making comparisons,
there must be contradictory words
in order to return and listen to them.
If you want to hear their voice, feign silence;
if you want to expand, feign contraction;
if you want to elevate, feign lowering;
if you want to take, feign giving.
If you want to open up (someone's) true feelings,
use imitations and comparisons
to guide their words.
Similar voices call out to each other,
and genuine principles converge.
Some do it because of this,
some do it because of that,
some use it to serve superiors,
some use it to manage subordinates.
This is how to listen for truth and falsehood, know sameness and difference,
To obtain their true feelings and deceptions.
Actions, speech, silence,
Accord or conflict with this,
Joy and anger can be seen through this pattern,
All use pre-determined rules as a standard.
Use repeated questioning to seek verification,
Observe what they rely on.
Therefore, those who use this,
Must keep themselves calm and still,
In order to listen to their words,
Investigate their affairs,
Evaluate all things,
Distinguish the strong from the weak.
Even if it's not their affair,
Seeing the subtle, know the type.
As if probing someone and residing within them,
Measuring their abilities,
Guessing their intentions.
The correspondence will not be missed,
Like the direction pointed by the *téng shé* serpent,
Like the arrow drawn by Yì.
Therefore, knowing begins with oneself,
Knowing oneself and then knowing others.
Understanding each other,
Is like the *bǐ mù* fish;
Observing their words,
Is like sound and echo;
Their manifestation is
like light and shadow.
Their scrutiny of words never misses,
like a lodestone attracting a needle,
a tongue picking out burnt bone.
Their interaction with people is subtle,
their perception of feelings is swift.
Like shadow and light,
like light and shadow;
like circle and square,
like square and circle.
Before the form is revealed,
use the circle to guide it;
once the form is revealed,
use the square to manage it.
Advance, retreat, left, right,
use this to control them.
If oneself is not first settled,
the shepherd will not be upright,
affairs will be unskillfully managed;
this is called forgetting the true state and losing the Way.
If oneself carefully settles things first to shepherd the people,
strategizing without showing form,
such that no one sees the gateway to it,
this is called being a heavenly spirit.
*Nèi Qián* Third
In the affairs between ruler and minister, superior and subordinate,
There are those who are distant yet intimate,
and those who are near yet estranged.
Approached, they are of no use;
departed, they are sought after again.
One advances daily, but is not received;
one is heard of from afar, and is longed for.
All matters have internal *jiàn* [latches or catches],
originally formed from inherent connections.
Some are connected by morality and virtue (*dàodé*),
some are connected by political allies and friends (*dǎngyǒu*),
some are connected by wealth and goods (*cáihuò*),
and some are connected by attractive appearance (*cǎisè*).
Employing their intentions,
if you wish to enter, then enter;
if you wish to exit, then exit;
if you wish to be intimate, then be intimate;
if you wish to be estranged, then be estranged;
if you wish to approach, then approach;
if you wish to depart, then depart;
if you wish to seek, then seek;
if you wish to long for, then long for.
Like an ant mother (*tiě mǔ*) following her young,
exiting without a gap,
entering without a trace,
going alone and coming alone,
no one is able to stop it.
"Internal" refers to presenting persuasive arguments;
*Qián* means to scheme and plan.
Those who wish to persuade
should strive to conceal their true intentions;
those who plan affairs
should strive to follow established principles.
Consider secretly what is possible and what is not,
openly discuss gains and losses,
in order to control their will.
Be prepared for what is coming at the right time,
in order to match their schemes.
Carefully consider future schemes,
and responses should be timely and appropriate.
Now, if internally there are disagreements,
it cannot be put into practice.
Therefore, carefully assess what is suitable for the time,
act according to what is convenient,
in order to seek change.
Using change to probe internal matters
is like examining and obtaining *qián*.
When speaking about the past,
first use compliant language;
when speaking about the future,
use transformative language.
Those skilled in transformation
carefully understand the terrain,
and then connect with the heavens to transform the four seasons,
causing ghosts and spirits to conform to yin and yang, thereby governing the people.
Observe their planned affairs,
Knowing their aspirations.
When affairs do not align,
there is something not yet understood.
When aligned but not solidified,
there is apparent intimacy but secret estrangement.
When affairs do not align,
the sage does not offer counsel.
Therefore, to be distant and yet intimate
indicates hidden virtue;
to be near and yet estranged
indicates incompatible aspirations;
to approach and yet be unheeded
indicates ineffective strategies;
to depart and yet be sought again
indicates that affairs originate from within;
to advance daily but remain unaccepted
indicates incompatible implementations;
to long for someone upon hearing their voice from afar
indicates alignment in planning,
awaiting decisive action.
Therefore it is said:
"To advise someone without understanding their kind
will encounter resistance;
to advise someone without grasping their situation
will encounter disapproval.
Grasping their situation
enables one to devise strategies.
With this, one can advance and retreat,
"Can be opened, can be closed."
Therefore, when a sage establishes affairs,
he uses this to first know and secure all things.
It originates from morality (dàodé), benevolence and righteousness (rényì), ritual and music (lǐyuè), and strategies and plans (jìmóu);
first select from the *Classic of Poetry* (*Shī*) and the *Classic of Documents* (*Shū*),
discuss comprehensively gains and losses,
debate about acceptance and rejection.
Those whom you want to unite with, employ internal methods;
those whom you want to remove, employ external methods.
Those skilled in internal and external methods must understand the principles of calculation;
assess and plan for forthcoming events,
resolve doubts when they appear,
so that plans are never miscalculated,
and merit is established and virtue built.
Managing reputations and accumulating wealth,
is called "securing and internally harmonizing."
If the ruler is foolish and does not govern,
and subordinates are in chaos and do not awaken,
then secure and reverse them.
Internally achieve self-attainment and externally do not linger,
persuade and let them fly away.
If fate comes of its own accord,
welcome and control it;
if it wishes to depart,
then give it what it wants in a time of crisis.
Revolve and transform in response to circumstances,
so that no one knows what you are doing,
Retreat becomes a great principle.
Chapter Four: Countering Flaws
Things have their own natural course,
matters have combinations and separations.
There are things near that cannot be seen,
and things far away that can be known.
That which is near and cannot be seen
is due to not examining its words;
that which is far away and can be known
is due to reversing back to verify the future.
A *xī* 巇 is a crack;
a crack is a fissure;
a fissure becomes a large gap.
When a *xī* 巇 first shows signs,
it can be countered and blocked,
it can be countered and turned back,
it can be countered and stopped,
it can be countered and concealed,
it can be countered and obtained.
This is called the principle of countering *xī* 巇.
The danger of affairs,
the sage knows it,
and preserves its use alone.
Based on changes, explain affairs,
thoroughly understand plans,
to recognize the subtle and minute,
It originates from the tip of an autumn hair,
yet its effect is wielded at the base of Mount Tài.
Its application externally
heralds plans of budding sprouts and shoots,
all stemming from exploiting cracks.
Exploiting cracks and fissures is the method of the Dao.
The world is in disarray,
there is no enlightened ruler above;
dukes and marquises lack morality,
therefore petty men are slanderous and villainous,
the worthy are not employed,
sages flee and hide,
those who are greedy for profit and deceitful rise,
ruler and ministers deceive each other,
the state crumbles and disintegrates,
and they attack and shoot at each other.
Fathers and sons are separated and scattered,
taking advantage of the chaos, they turn against each other;
this is called "budding sprouts and fissures".
When a sage sees budding sprouts and fissures,
he counters them with the law.
If the world can be governed,
then he counters and blocks them;
if it cannot be governed,
then he counters and obtains benefit from them.
Sometimes the countering is like this,
sometimes the countering is like that;
Or to resist and oppose them;
or to resist and overturn them.
In the governance of the Five Emperors,
resistance was used to obstruct;
in the affairs of the Three Kings,
resistance was used to achieve success.
Among the feudal lords, mutual resistance
was beyond counting.
In times like these,
being able to resist is advantageous.
is a sage.
From the joining and separation, the beginning and end of Heaven and Earth,
there must be cracks and fissures,
which cannot be ignored.
Examine them with *bāihé* (opening and closing),
and one who can use this method
A sage
is an envoy of Heaven and Earth.
If there is nothing in the world to resist,
then lie low and await the time;
if the time is such that there is something to resist,
then devise a plan for it.
You can align with those above,
and control those below.
If you can adapt and follow the course of things,
you will be guarding the spirit of Heaven and Earth.
Chapter Five: Flying Clamps
Generally, gauging (dù) authority, measuring (quán) capabilities, and assessing (liáng) potential are
the means by which to attract those from afar and bring near those close by.
To establish power (shì) and control affairs,
one must first observe groups of like-minded and dissenting individuals,
distinguish between statements of right and wrong,
understand the language of those within and without (the court),
know the quantities of what exists and what does not,
decide on plans for security and danger,
determine matters of closeness and distance (between people),
and only then gauge and measure them.
That which is hidden and encompasses
can then be investigated,
can then be sought,
can then be used.
Employ the language of drawing in (gōu) and clamping down (qián),
swiftly clamp them down.
The speech of drawing in and clamping down,
its manner of speaking
is sometimes similar, sometimes different.
That which should not be done well:
sometimes first investigate it,
and then repeatedly burden them;
sometimes first weigh them down with burdens,
and then destroy them;
sometimes one takes repeated burdens as destruction,
sometimes one takes destruction as repeated burdens.
Its application:
Some use wealth and goods, extraordinary objects, pearls and jade, flawless jade, and vibrant colors to serve them.
Some assess their capabilities and establish influence to ensnare them.
Some lie in wait, observing gaps and cracks, and then seize them,
using these methods to exploit vulnerabilities.
When one intends to employ these methods on a grand scale throughout the realm,
one must assess authority and measure capabilities,
observe the waxing and waning of opportune times,
determine the extent of the terrain,
the ease or difficulty of dangerous passes,
the amount of the people's wealth and resources,
and the alliances of the feudal lords, who is close and who is distant,
who loves and who hates.
Discern their innermost thoughts and concerns,
scrutinize their intentions,
understand what they like and dislike,
and then address what they value,
using the words of the "flying clamp" to ensnare what they desire,
and seek it through clamping.
When employing it on individuals,
one must measure their intelligence and abilities, assess their talents and strength, and estimate their vigor and influence,
making oneself a pivot point for them,
to greet them and follow them,
to harmonize with them through clamping,
and to act appropriately according to their intentions.
This is the application of the "flying clamp."
When used on people,
Then empty goes and substance comes;
connect without losing;
thereby to investigate its wording.
It can be clamped and followed,
it can be clamped and traversed;
it can be drawn east,
it can be drawn west;
it can be drawn south,
it can be drawn north;
it can be drawn back,
it can be drawn over.
Though overturned, it can recover;
it does not lose its measure.
Chapter Six: Opposition and Agreement
In general, in inclining towards agreement, doubling back, and rebelling,
calculations must have things that are suitable.
Transformation, revolution, and cyclical connection
each has its own form and power.
Repeatedly seek each other,
make regulations according to circumstances.
Therefore, the sage dwells between Heaven and Earth,
establishes himself and governs the world,
dispensing instruction and proclaiming his name.
He must rely on the convergence of affairs and things,
observe the suitability of the seasons,
rely on what is much or little;
by this, he knows it in advance
and transform it.
The world has no constant nobility,
affairs have no constant teacher.
The sage constantly acts through non-action,
listens to everything.
Success lies in adapting to the affair and aligning with plans,
take the lead in it.
If it aligns with that side but separates from this side,
plans cannot be loyal to both sides,
there will inevitably be rebellion and opposition.
Rebelling against this,
opposing that;
opposing this,
rebelling against that.
The technique is,
if applying it to the world,
one must measure the world and act accordingly;
if applying it to a state,
one must measure the state and act accordingly;
if applying it to a family,
one must measure the family and act accordingly;
if applying it to oneself,
one must measure one's figure, talent, ability, and momentum and act accordingly.
In magnitude, progress, and retreat,
the principle of its application is the same.
One must first strategize and plan thoroughly,
and then implement it using the art of *fēi qián*.
In ancient times, those skilled at turning their backs or facing forward
could harmonize the four seas and encompass the various lords.
They went against or aligned with Heaven and Earth, transforming and altering them,
and then used this to seek agreement.
Thus, Yī Yǐn five times went to Tāng and five times went to Jié,
but could not make anything clear.
Then, he aligned with Tāng.
Lǚ Shàng three times went to Wén Wáng and three times entered Yīn,
but could not make anything clear.
Then, he aligned with Wén Wáng.
This is understanding the control of Heaven's mandate.
Therefore, returning to them was without doubt.
If one is not a most sage person who understands the profound,
one cannot govern the world;
if one does not labor one's mind and think arduously,
one cannot get to the source of affairs;
if one does not fully examine and see emotions,
one cannot achieve fame;
if one's material quality is not intelligent,
one cannot employ troops;
if loyalty and sincerity are without truth,
one cannot know people.
Therefore, in the way of going against or aligning,
one must first measure one's own talents, abilities, knowledge, and wisdom,
assess what lengths and shortcomings, distances and proximities, one is not as good at.
Only then can one advance,
only then can one retreat,
only then can one release,
Only then can one roam freely.
Chapter Seven: "Assessing"
Those of old who were skilled in employing the world [tiān xià],
invariably measured the power [quán] of the world,
and assessed the situations of the various lords [zhū hóu].
If measuring power [quán] is not discerning,
one will not know the proper terms for strength and weakness, lightness and heaviness;
if assessing situations is not discerning,
one will not know the hidden changes and movements.
What is meant by measuring power [quán]?
It means:
to estimate size,
to deliberate on numbers large and small.
To weigh the presence or absence of goods and wealth,
to calculate the number of people, their abundance or lack, how much surplus or deficiency there is;
to distinguish the advantageousness or disadvantageousness of terrain, what is beneficial and what is harmful;
to consider the length or shortness of planning;
the closeness or distance, worthiness or unworthiness of ruler and ministers;
the fewness or numerousness of wise and discerning guests;
to observe the fortune and misfortune, auspiciousness and inauspiciousness of the seasons;
which of the lords [zhū hóu] are to be used and which are not;
which changes in the people's [bǎi xìng] hearts are peaceful or dangerous,
what they like and what they hate,
which are convenient for treachery.
One who can know these things
is said to have measured power [quán].
To assess situations, one must go when they are extremely happy
Going to the extreme to fulfill their desires,
when they have desires,
they cannot conceal their true feelings.
Always in their most fearful moments,
going to the extreme to expose their detestation,
when they have detestation,
they cannot conceal their true feelings.
Desires and feelings will inevitably lose their constancy.
Those who are moved but do not understand this inconstancy,
will surely mistake the person.
Do not speak with them, but inquire further of their close associates,
to understand what brings them comfort.
Indeed, when feelings change internally,
their form is revealed externally.
Therefore, one must always use what is visible to understand what is hidden.
This is why it is called gauging depths and assessing feelings.
Therefore, when planning affairs of state,
one must carefully consider power and measure capacity;
when persuading a ruler,
one must carefully assess their feelings.
Schemes and considerations regarding feelings and desires
must arise from this.
Only then can one be valued,
only then can one be despised,
only then can one be held in high regard,
only then can one be held lightly,
only then can one bring benefit,
Thus, it can be harmed;
thus, it can be achieved;
thus, it can be defeated.
The principle for these is the same.
Therefore, even with the doctrines of former kings and the plans of sages,
without gauging emotions and concealing intentions,
there is no way to obtain what you seek.
This is the great foundation of planning,
and the method of persuasion.
Always have matters involving others,
and let no one precede you.
To arrive before things happen
is the most difficult thing to do.
Therefore, it is said, "Gauging emotions is the most difficult to guard and control."
Words must be timely concerning his plans,
therefore, observe even the smallest movements,
for there is nothing without benefit or harm,
and from this, beautiful achievements can arise.
Creating achievements is the power of opportunity.
This is about gauging emotions and embellishing words,
forming well-structured arguments before discussing them.
Chapter Eight: Mó Piān (Assessing)
Mó (Assessing) is a symbol.
Nèi Fú (Internal Symbol) is the master of gauging.
Using it has its way,
and its way must be hidden.
Subtly assess them with what they desire,
Measure and probe it,
the inner accord will surely respond.
Its response
must have a cause.
Therefore, subtly remove it;
this is called blocking loopholes, hiding clues, concealing appearances, and escaping emotions,
so that people do not know.
Thus, one can accomplish their task without worry.
Gaging is here,
conformity is there.
Following this and responding accordingly,
nothing is impossible.
The skillful gagers of old
were like holding a hook and facing a deep abyss.
If you bait and cast it,
you will surely catch fish.
Therefore, it is said:
“The ruler's affairs are accomplished daily, yet people do not know;
the ruler's army wins daily, yet people are not afraid."
The sage plans in secret;
therefore, it is called "divine";
he achieves it openly;
therefore, it is called "obvious."
What is meant by "the ruler's affairs are accomplished daily"
is accumulating virtue,
and the people are at peace,
not knowing why they benefit;
Accumulating goodness,
the people are guided by it,
without knowing why it is so;
and the world compares it to the gods.
The one who "commands troops and wins daily"
constantly wages war without contention or expenditure,
yet the people do not know why they submit,
do not know why they fear,
and the world compares him to the gods.
Those who probe (mó 摩) others
do so by means of tranquility,
by means of uprightness,
by means of joy,
by means of anger,
by means of reputation,
by means of action,
by means of incorruptibility,
by means of trustworthiness,
by means of profit,
by means of humility.
Tranquility is stillness,
uprightness is straightforwardness,
joy is delight,
anger is agitation,
reputation is manifestation,
action is accomplishment,
incorruptibility is purity,
Trustworthiness is clarity;
Profit is seeking;
Humility is flattery.
Therefore, that which the sage uniquely employs,
all people possess;
yet those who achieve no success,
it is because their use of it is incorrect.
Therefore, nothing is more difficult than thorough planning,
nothing is more difficult than complete listening,
nothing is more difficult than ensuring success in affairs;
these three things can only be achieved through attrition (introspection, testing).
Therefore, planning must desire thoroughness,
one must select those with whom to communicate when persuading.
Therefore, it is said:
"Perhaps bind and have no gap."
Now, the success of an affair must align with calculation,
therefore it is said:
"The ways of calculation and the times are things that are coupled together.”

or might encounter being sorrowful and constantly trying to improve themselves,
or might encounter failing repeatedly to establish themselves.
Therefore, the Dao values controlling others,
and not being controlled by others.
The one who controls others holds power,
and the one who is controlled by others loses their life.
Therefore, observing shapes creates appearance,
and imitating forms creates countenance,
hearing sounds harmonizes tones,
understanding enmity resolves disputes,
gathering departing words,
and focusing the mind preserves righteousness.
The main principle in recording events is recording the principles and numbers of the Dao,
whose changes are essential in the "Chí Shū (持樞)" and "Zhōng Jīng (中經)."
"Observing shapes creates appearance,
and imitating forms creates countenance,"
means that the Yáo (爻, lines in the *Yì Jīng*) are the masters of this,
which can be obtained through influence, description, appearance, and countenance.
A person who has something to protect,
does not look at what is improper,
does not listen to what is evil,
always speaks of the *Shī* (詩, Classic of Poetry) and *Shū* (書, Classic of Documents),
Conduct is not deviant or licentious,
taking the Dào as its form,
and listening as its countenance.
Appearance is solemn, and expression is gentle.
It cannot be acquired through imitation of appearance.
In this way, hidden feelings and divisions can be blocked and eliminated.
Listening to sounds and harmonizing tones
means that if the tones and breaths are not in harmony, then favor and affection will not connect.
Therefore, *shāng* and *jiǎo* do not combine,
and *zhǐ* and *yǔ* do not pair.
Who can be the master of the four tones?
Only *gōng*, perhaps?
Therefore, if the tones are not harmonious,
then there is no grief.
Therefore, voices that are scattered, hurtful, ugly, and damaging
will certainly be offensive to the ear.
Even if there are beautiful actions and great reputations,
they cannot rely on each other like the eyes of the *bǐmù* bird or wings joined together,
because this is a case of breath not harmonizing and tones not being in tune.
Resolving enmity and fighting in rifts
means resolving the enmity of the weak.
Fighting in rifts means fighting against the strong.
Once the strong fight in the rifts,
the one who claims victory exalts their achievement and magnifies their power.
The weak one laments their defeat,
grieves over their lowliness,
To sully their reputation,
to disgrace their ancestry.
Therefore, the victor contends on the power of their momentum,
advancing recklessly without knowing when to retreat.
The weak lament their defeats upon hearing of them,
and seeing their wounds redoubles their strength;
they would rather die than yield.
If there is no ultimate greatness in the crevices (xiè),
and no formidable strength to resist,
then all can be threatened and annexed.
"Stringing together those who leave" means to string together words that relate to one's own connections,
in order to leave room for further consideration.
Therefore, in dealing with those who are upright and trustworthy, praise their conduct and encourage their ambition,
say that what can be done can be done again,
and express joy at the prospect of meeting them.
Use the opinions of many people
to draw inferences and connect to the past,
clarify doubts and dispel them.
"Rejecting words" means observing and searching for shortcomings.
Therefore, many words inevitably contain some shortcomings;
recognize these shortcomings and examine them.
Incite them with taboos,
show them timely prohibitions,
so that people become fearful because of them.
Then, establish trust to reassure their minds,
collect their words, conceal and reject them,
never revealing to diverse people your own shortcomings.
"Se She Xin" (攝心, Capturing the Mind) means that when encountering someone who is fond of learning skills and techniques,
one should praise them from afar.
Then test them,
surprising them with the strange and unusual,
causing people to attach their minds to oneself.
Verify it through testing,
and after the testing, disturb their established notions.
I return to sincerity within myself.
When encountering those who indulge in lust and alcohol,
perform for them arts and music,
and move them with the thought of certain death,
and the worries of diminishing lifespan.
Delight them with things they have not seen themselves,
so that in the end, they can contemplate the boundlessness of fate,
making them anticipate a future encounter.
"Shou Yi" (守義, Upholding Righteousness) means upholding righteousness based on human principles,
probing the mind inwardly to achieve agreement.
"Tan Xin" (探心, Probing the Mind) means probing to find their master.
Controlling the internal from the external,
affairs have connections and follow accordingly.
Therefore, when a petty person compares themselves to others,
they resort to deviant methods and employ them,
to the point of being able to ruin families and seize states.
Without virtuous wisdom, one cannot uphold a family with righteousness,
nor can one uphold a state with the Way.
What the sage values in the subtlety of the Way
Truly, it is that which can transform danger into safety,
rescue ruin and cause survival.
*Guǐ Gǔzi* Lost Writings
For a person to be not good, and yet able to correct it,
is difficult.
If persuasion does not succeed,
and words are not followed,
it is because the argument is not clear.
If it is already clear and yet not acted upon,
it is because the holding to it is not firm.
If it is already firm and yet not acted upon,
it is because it has not yet struck what is good in his heart.
Argue it, clarify it, hold to it, make it firm,
and also strike what that person considers good,
then the words will be miraculous and treasured.
They will be clear and distinct.
They will be able to enter into the heart of the person.
If with all this, persuasion still does not succeed,
such a thing has never been heard of under heaven.
Therefore, it is said:
The sage is imperishable;
adapting to changing times is what he guards.
Emptiness is the constant principle of the Dao,
and reliance is the guiding principle of the ruler.
Tián Chéngzǐ killed the ruler of Qí,
and after twelve generations, possessed the state of Qí.
Serving a sagacious ruler, there is obedience and compliance,
without remonstrance;
serving a mediocre ruler, there is remonstrance,
without flattery;
serving a tyrannical ruler, there is amendment and reduction,
without dissimulation.
If the ruler gains renown, then the ministers rely on him;
if the ruler loses renown, then the ministers deceive him.
When others move, I remain still;
when others speak, I listen;
ability to retain and ability to dismiss [officials],
depend on me asking [about them].
Understanding human nature leads to fewer burdens,
understanding destiny leads to no worries.
When worries and burdens are gone, then the mind is at peace;
when the mind is at peace, then benevolence and righteousness are manifested.
To nourish the people with virtue
is like grass and trees obtaining their proper season;
To transform people with benevolence
, is like Heaven producing grass and trees
, and moistening them with rain and dew.
During the Zhōu 周 dynasty, there was a prominent man of virtue who lived in seclusion in Guǐ Gǔ 鬼谷,
calling himself Guǐ Gǔ Zǐ 鬼谷子,
to indicate his remoteness.
However, the name "Guǐ Gǔ 鬼谷"
is a common name for recluses.
During the Zhōu 周 dynasty, there was a prominent man of virtue residing in Guǐ Gǔ 鬼谷,
called Master Guǐ Gǔ 鬼谷先生.
Sū Qín 蘇秦 and Zhāng Yí 張儀 went to see him.
The Master said:
"I will explain the ultimate Dao 道 to you two.
You should fast and purify yourselves, and choose an auspicious day to learn."
Later, Qín 秦 and Yí 儀 fasted and purified themselves and went.
Sū Qín 蘇秦 wished to mystify his Dao 道,
therefore, he assumed the name Guǐ Gǔ 鬼谷.
